subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a separate heartbeat execution lane or worker, or keep the current serialized/deferred heartbeat model with narrower retry and idle mitigations?
rationale: Current code intentionally uses shared runner, wake, reply, session, and delivery paths; changing that boundary affects ordering, session state, and tool side effects, so automation should not choose the permanent architecture.

options.title: Design An Isolated Heartbeat Lane
options.body: Define session-state, delivery-ordering, retry, and tool-side-effect contracts before implementing independent heartbeat execution.

options.title: Keep Serialized Heartbeats
options.body: Retain the current skip-and-retry model and focus on narrower mitigations such as retry delay, idle gating, and lighter heartbeat context.

options.title: Defer Until Live Repro
options.body: Wait for live channel proof of the stall severity before accepting architecture work beyond the existing retry-cadence fixes.

recommendation.title: Design An Isolated Heartbeat Lane
recommendation.body: Define session-state, delivery-ordering, retry, and tool-side-effect contracts before implementing independent heartbeat execution.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the central heartbeat runner history and the related requests-in-flight drift change, making him the strongest routing candidate for the architecture choice.
